page: Microsoft Azure E16pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the arm64 architecture, powered by a 16-core Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. The instance features a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation without simultaneous multithreading, providing 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs. The processor subsystem includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB, establishing an 8.0 GB per core ratio, accompanied by a bundled 945 GB local NVMe solid-state drive.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional memory performance alongside consistent general-purpose compute throughput. In PassMark memory testing, the instance achieved a top-tier placement in the top 10 percent with a score of 3369.15. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 304.72 GB/sec and write bandwidth reached 123.05 GB/sec, placing both in the top 25 percent. Compute scores, including Geekbench multi-core at 14685.0 and stress-ng multi-core at 33147.69, reflect standard mid-tier execution. Single-threaded gzip compression scored in the top 25 percent at 33.05 GB/sec, while specialized tasks like medium-model LLM prompt processing demonstrated lower relative throughput.

The combination of dedicated ARM execution cores, high-bandwidth memory, and integrated NVMe scratch storage makes this instance cost-effective for memory-intensive workloads that benefit from ARM efficiency. Typical fits include in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, large-scale data transformation, and memory-constrained analytical processing pipelines that require predictable memory latency without the overhead of hardware accelerator configurations.
